title: authfile_load sizes its buffer to the file's exact length, so fgets writes the terminating NUL one byte past it
object: auth_data, one calloc(1, sb.st_size) holding the whole --auth-file
lifetime_ender: NONE -- the buffer is alive throughout. This corpus's rows are spatial by construction.
shape: a line that exactly fills the allocation makes fgets's terminating NUL land one byte past it
allocator_layer: the system allocator itself: one calloc, no inner layer. That is what makes this the NOT-NESTED spatial row.
fidelity: real allocator, model consumer. calloc and free are the platform's own, and the arms differ by exactly the upstream fix (sb.st_size versus sb.st_size + 1). fgets is reduced to the write C requires of it -- for a line shorter than the size argument and ending at EOF it stores the line's bytes and then a terminating NUL -- so the crossing sits on the corpus's labelled probe rather than inside libc. Nothing about WHERE the NUL lands is reduced; that is the defect. The fix's other two hunks (an auth_end clamp on the fgets length, and a '\0' break in the entry scan) bound LATER lines and are left out, which PROVENANCE.md states.
live_proof: the fix is an ancestor of the 1.6.45 tag (git merge-base --is-ancestor ddee3e2 1.6.45 succeeds), and 1.6.45:authfile.c:50 reads 'auth_data = calloc(1, sb.st_size + 2);' -- the fixed form, two past rather than the pre-fix exact size. The case reconstructs the pre-fix consumer shape against the shipped allocator, the convention stated at ../../allocator-repros/README.md:132-135 and carried by 27 of the 33 cases in this tree.
distinguishing: the arms differ by ONE term, the + 1 in the allocation size. Everything else -- the line, its length, the write offset -- is identical, so a changed reading is attributable to the fix and to nothing else.

cheribsd-revocation.target: stock CheriBSD purecap with libc revocation on
cheribsd-revocation.oracle:
MEASURED 2026-10-06 on this host: the sequence COMPLETES. **NOT CAUGHT, which REFUTES this arm's prediction.** The crossing is one byte past calloc(1, 9), and CheriBSD's malloc hands out a capability whose length is the allocator's USABLE SIZE, not the request: measured in the same guest, calloc(1,1) and calloc(1,9) both return length=16, calloc(1,17) returns 32, calloc(1,8192) returns exactly 8192. Offset 9 is therefore inside the bounds and no fault is possible. the platform's own bounds control fired in the same boot: cheribsd-bounds runs abi-probe oob, which sets bounds to exactly 16 and reads offset 16, and it PASSED alongside cheribsd-abi reporting CHERI_ABI pointer_bytes=16 runtime_revocation=1. A spatial completion is therefore a reading, not a silent detector. Attribution: not established -- SUPERVISE reported 'expect read_probe unavailable', and this corpus's probe is a static write_probe duplicated across case.c and driver.c. Moot here, since nothing faulted. RE-MEASURED 2026-10-07 by the committed runner, results/20261007-cheribsd/: NOT CAUGHT -- the sequence completes and prints VERDICT DEFECT-REPRODUCED, exit status 0. This CONFIRMS the refutation recorded on 2026-10-06 rather than re-deriving it: the crossing is one byte past calloc(1, 9) and CheriBSD's malloc bounds to the allocator's USABLE size, so a 9-byte request yields a 16-byte capability and offset 9 is inside the bounds. supervise resolved `expect mch_write_probe 0x102396`, so the probe was found and simply never faulted. ATTRIBUTION IS NOW ESTABLISHED, which it was not before. This corpus declared its probe `static` in shared/corpus.h until 2026-10-07, so every translation unit had a private copy and supervise reported the symbol unavailable -- the reason this row read 'attribution: not established'. The probe is now DECLARED in the header and DEFINED ONCE in shared/driver.c. Proven inert: the native runner was re-run afterwards and its verdict summary is unchanged (plain=reproduced, asan-buggy=heap-buffer-overflow, asan-fixed=silent). The platform controls fired in the same boot: cheribsd-abi reported `CHERI_ABI pointer_bytes=16 runtime_revocation=1` and cheribsd-bounds reported CHERI_BOUNDARY_READY, both PASS, and the committed runner refuses to report a suite whose controls did not fire (exit 75) rather than letting an empty boot read as a result.

RE-MEASURED 2026-10-08 in the same vehicle: MEASURED 2026-10-08, results/2026-10-08-cheribsd/: **NOT CAUGHT, and clean here is NOT a negative result about the defect.** The sequence COMPLETES, exit status 0, with supervise resolving `expect mch_write_probe 0x1023be` from the ELF -- so the probe was found and simply never faulted. THE MECHANISM: malloc bounds a capability to the allocator's USABLE size and not to the request, so a crossing shorter than the gap to the next size class stays inside the same allocation and no capability check can see it. This is a property of the allocator's granularity, not of the bug. tools/size-class-audit.py reports this case ABSORBED from the measured request size, and the two agree. The Capstone arms are the discriminating ones here.
